author: viveris
engine_flags: llama-bench pp512/tg128; MTP3; vLLM speculative mtp7; DFlash2 dflash7
decode_tps: llama.cpp tg128 81 tok/s; 140 tok/s with MTP3 (mtp-bench); vLLM baseline 72 tok/s; mtp7 157 tok/s; dflash7 215 tok/s; DFlash2 just under 300 tok/s on code_python
prefill_or_ttft: llama.cpp pp512 3,920 tok/s; vLLM NVFP4 prefill ~13,000 tok/s
command_or_config: llama-bench / mtp-bench on llama.cpp and vLLM
quote: A basic llama-bench on Qwen 3.8 27B UD-Q4_K_M gives pp512 3920 tok/s / tg128 81 tok/s on a 500W RTX PRO 6000. With MTP3 this is 140 tok/s on mtp-bench.
caveats: Story thread: M5 Ultra Mac Studio review.

author: snehesht
quote: On my machine (Nvidia 4090, 128GB DDR5, Ryzen 7950x3d) I'm getting 124 tokens per sec, thought to share it here.
caveats: Story OP (same author) claims 100T/s on 4090.

author: mrinterweb
decode_tps: > 110 tokens/sec (3 token MTP); reference: their Qwen 3.8 q5 27B ~60 TPS
quote: I have 1x RTX 4090 (24GB VRAM) and 128GB DDR4 RAM. I am seeing > 110 tokens/sec (3 token MTP). Using 60K/260k context currently.

author: latentsea
hardware: AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 32GB + 64GB RAM
quote: now with Strata on an R9700 and 64GB of RAM I can run Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS at 60 t/s
caveats: AMD single-card gap hardware.

author: Tade0
quote: I managed to get a context of 195k for Qwen3.5-9b Q4_K_M using a llama.cpp fork that supports TurboQuant ... Speed remains the main limitation, as IIRC I was getting ~26-30tps on a 7700S
caveats: 'IIRC' figure; old AMD APU gap hardware.

author: commenter
quote: Using llama.cpp with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B or gemma4-26B-A4B gets me 200-300 tokens/s on prompt processing and 20-40 t/s output
caveats: 'It took a lot of parameter fiddling to get it to that speed' — flags not given. 6GB-VRAM gap hardware.

author: commenter
quote: Two arc b60s. The intel vllm build is getting me ~15t/s decode with heavy context using qwen3.8 27b.
caveats: Intel Arc gap hardware.

author: aziis98
model: ds4/dwarfstar runner; poster separately extracts Qwen3.5-4B-MTP+SYCL
quote: Just tried this on my Intel Ultra 7 255H, I also only have an iGPU. This does ~22tps!
caveats: 22tps is the ds4go/dwarfstar run, not a Qwen model run; poster's extracted qwen3.5 4b mtp + sycl single-file runner is unverified quality. Intel iGPU gap hardware.

author: commenter
decode_tps: 55tok/s (1 user); ~35tok/s per user at 5 simultaneous users
prefill_or_ttft: 1500 prefill (1 user); 650 per user at 5 users
quote: It runs at 55tok/s 1500 prefill for one user at a time, and about 35tok/s 650 prefill per user for 5 simultaneous users.
caveats: Cheap 6x3090 multi-GPU rig gap hardware; no engine/flags.

author: Winfred-zz
decode_tps: Strata 40 to 60 t/s after tweaking; 'Standard Qwen 3.8 runs at 20 t/s, this modified [ninfer] version can do 50 t/s'
quote: Yet with some tweaking and optimizing I still manage to get strata to run at 40 to 60 t/s.
caveats: Includes 128-task code quality table (Strata 89.1% vs ninfer 71.9%).

author: commenter
quote: # lmstudio-community/qwen3.8-27b@q4_k_m decode falloff 104.3 tok/s @ 12,683 -> 55.8 tok/s @ 240,755 (53% retained); # qwen3_8_27b_nvfp4.ninfer decode falloff 173.3 tok/s @ 11,867 -> 139.3 tok/s @ 225,710 (80% retained)
caveats: Single-user; poster says more headroom (no overclock attempted).

author: commenter
engine_flags: SYCL with Intel optimizations; Vulkan backend also tested
quote: On a Laptop with 32 GB RAM and Iris Xe integrated graphic card, I get between 11-18 Tokens/Second with Qwen 3.8 27B and llama.cpp with sysl Intel optimisations.
caveats: Vulkan same speed but occasional segfaults. Intel iGPU gap hardware.

author: deepanwadhwa
quote: I am running Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on my 16GB M3 and get 7-8 tokens/sec with all the optimizations while keeping the peak memory and thermal warnings at check.
caveats: 16GB Mac gap hardware.

author: commenter
quote: I see more like 30-35t/s on a 16" M5 Max using 3.8:27b Q4, regardless of whether it's mlx or gguf. qwen3.5:122b-a10b is significantly faster at around 60-65.
caveats: Counters the 40 tok/s in the review article.

author: commenter
decode_tps: rapid-mlx: 175 tok/s; Magnitude: 161 tok/s (mixed Qwen set)
prefill_or_ttft: TTFT 64 ms vs 111 ms; ~760-token cold prefill 594 ms vs 669 ms
quote: VIA rapid-mlx :8902 (MLX) Decode: 175 tok/s TTFT: 64 ms prefill (~760 tok cold): 594 ms; Magnitude 0.2.1 (GGUF/llama.cpp+Rust) Decode: 161 tok/s TTFT: 111 ms prefill (~760 tok cold): 669 ms
caveats: Averages over multiple models; poster's conclusion: engine adds little for already-optimized Qwen models.

author: commenter
decode_tps: Qwen3.6 MoE: 30 t/s typical; Qwen3.8: 4-9 t/s typical
prefill_or_ttft: Qwen3.6: 500 t/s peak; Qwen3.8: 150 t/s peak
quote: The Moe 3.6 on my setup is much faster, 500t/s peaks, 30t/s typical, vs 3.8 150 peak, 4-9 t/s typical.
caveats: Peaks read as prompt-processing peaks; typical = decode. Mac 64GB lane.

author: commenter
decode_tps: Intel claimed ~1400 tok/s generation for Qwen3.6-moe on Arc B70; commenter found the setup was 200 concurrent users on the same 1024-token prompt (poster estimate: <150 tok/s single-user)
quote: I believe Intel has claimed something like 1400tok/s (generation! Not prefill) of Qwen3.6-moe on Arc b70. ... Turns out it was 200 simultaneous users running the same 1024 token prompt :D
caveats: Second-hand vendor claim + community debunk; Intel Arc gap hardware.

author: commenter
quote: I get up to 90 tokens / second with Jundot/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-oQ6-mtp, on a M3 Max with 64GB. ... don't bother quanting your KV Cache (don't enable turboquant in oMLX), since that will slow you down.
caveats: Story: Qwen 3.6 easier to run on Mac (JetBrains). Same checkpoint cited in 49690588: ~90 toks/sec M3 Max.

author: jakelsaunders94
command_or_config: blog: self-hosted sandboxed agentic software factory
quote: Using a RTX 5090 ($3~4k), I can run Qwen 3.8 27B at ~180 TPS with ninfer [0].

author: commenter
quote: I run Gemma 4 31B and Qwen 3.6 27B on my dual 32GB GPU setup (cheap old Radeon Pro V620 GPUs) at about 20 t/s, which is not fast enough for comfortable interactive agentic use.
caveats: Cheap multi-GPU gap hardware; poster elsewhere runs Qwen3.8-27B on the same rig.

author: commenter
hardware: AMD Ryzen AI Halo (Strix Halo reference, 128GB)

quote: vLLM gives me ~7000+ tok/sec with Gemma 4's MoE model. Vs ~6000 tok/sec for Qwen 3.6 MoE.
